domain: AI workloads and algorithms, 2026-2100+, as they constrain the Dyson-swarm compute architecture (study 5 of 8)
summary: WORKLOADS 2026-2100+. Durable properties to design a swarm around, all measured: forward-pass generation dominates. Self-play, RL rollouts and serving take 50-92 % of compute, and inference went 26 % -> ~50 % -> ~67 % (2024-2026). Most training compute is many experiments: final runs were ~7 % of OpenAI's 2024 compute. Per-sequence working state stays ~1-70 GB because KV/token fell x0.35/yr while context grew x3/yr. Training state per FLOP falls (N~C^0.5). Sparsity rose 3.6 -> 32. Critical batch grows as D^0.38-0.47. Low-comm methods cut traffic 100-1,000x but are proven only to 4.75e23 FLOP and M<=8-16 replicas. Agents need general-purpose sandboxes: CPU:GPU went 1:8 -> 1:4, forecast 1:1-1:2. The human text stock (3e14 tokens) is exhausted by a single 2070 sail-year run. SHAPE: the sail (14.8 MW, 1.5e21/5.7e21/1.1e22 FLOP/s, 0.1/0.85/3.4 EB) is the synchronous unit. A 2070 sail trains a 7e28-FLOP, ~1e13-active (7e14 total) model per year using 0.5 % of its memory. It serves ~1.35e7 agents (6.7e8 tok/s, 1.4x Google 2025) and decodes a 1e12-active model single-stream at ~4.7e4 tok/s, as fast as a pod. Cross-sail DiLoCo/SparseLoCo needs only 1e-4-4e-2 of a sail's laser capacity, so the limit is the replica penalty. 1e2-1e5 sails may give 3e30-8e32 effective FLOP/yr (speculative), and the largest coherent learner+actor enterprise is <=1e-9 of a 3.4e16-sail swarm. The swarm is therefore a population: ~1e23-1e25 agent streams, ~2e23 (2e21-2e25) human-brain-equivalents at f=0.01/2070, searches, self-play, ensembles and science (60-230 exascale machines per sail). POD SHARE from workloads: 12.8 % (7.8-24.5) in 2040, 2.7 % (1.6-5.7) in 2070 and 1.1 % (0.55-2.4) in 2100+ when combined with studies 2-3. That is ~2.5x their 5/1/0.3 % because agent tool/environment CPU work is rising. It stays ~15 % (6-33 %) forever unless film chiplets get a sandbox-capable core + MMU + NVM main memory, which is worth 10-30 % of swarm mass. Pods are for dies >~3.8 W, radiation-intolerant memory, cryogenics and archives, never for synchronous work. The user's intuition holds if 'satellite' means the sail: concentration happens inside it via photonic lanes.

pod_share_by_era.workload_driven: 15 % (10-20 %): 5-10 % shielded CPU+DRAM/flash (sandboxes, RL environments, storage, switching) + 5-10 % HBM training/hedge islands
pod_share_by_era.reasons: architecture.md baseline; film has 16 MB/chiplet, no DRAM, electrical mesh only.

pod_share_by_era.mass_cost: each +1 % of power in pods adds 5.4 % to swarm mass (pod 4.09 vs film 0.638 g/W, study 4)
pod_share_by_era.reasons: Agent tool/environment CPU work is the largest pod driver: measured CPU:GPU went 1:8 -> 1:4 and is forecast 1:1-1:2, so CPU work is 7-40 % of power; in 2040 30-90 % of it still needs DRAM or fast cores because NVM-as-main-memory on the film is not yet mature (study 2: 2045-2070). Training hedge 0-3 % (photonic lanes nascent, MoE all-to-all 20 % of energy). Higher than study 2's 5 % because study 2 used the 2026 CPU share.

pod_share_by_era.mass_cost: each +1 % of power in pods adds 7.1 % to swarm mass (pod 4.02 vs film 0.497 g/W, study 4)
pod_share_by_era.reasons: MRAM/FeRAM main memory (8 GB/chiplet) and 0.15 W cores that match a 2026 server core leave only latency-critical single-thread work, write-heavy DRAM work and cryogenic/quantum devices: 3-25 % of a 5-40 % CPU share. Training needs no pods (state is 600x below sail memory). Storage 0.02-0.3 %.

pod_share_by_era.mass_cost: each +1 % of power in pods adds 7.4 % to swarm mass (pod 4.02 vs film 0.48 g/W, study 4)
pod_share_by_era.reasons: Residual: dies above ~3.8 W (fast single-thread cores, switch ASICs, cryostats), radiation-intolerant special memory, glass archives. 0.5-2.4 %.

pod_share_by_era.statement: Above ~3.8 W per die a pod beats the film per kg (film spreader mass ~0.94 g/W per W of die power vs pod 4.02 g/W); below it, everything goes on the film. If film chiplets are pure tensor engines (no general-purpose core, MMU and NVM main memory), the pod share stays ~15 % (6-33 %) in every era because agent environments need somewhere to run. Putting a sandbox-capable core on each chiplet (or 1 in N) is worth 10-30 % of swarm mass.

durable_properties.property: Generation dominates; learning is a small synchronous core
durable_properties.numbers: actor:learner 1:1 to 300:1 measured (AlphaZero ~92 % of power in self-play, INTELLECT-2 80 %, LLM RL rollouts 49-90+ % of time); inference 26 % -> ~50 % -> ~67 % of compute 2024-2026
durable_properties.design_consequence: 80-95 % of swarm FLOPs are forward passes that need no cross-sail coupling; design sails for batched decode with local memory, not for one global job.

durable_properties.property: Most R&D compute is many small experiments
durable_properties.numbers: OpenAI 2024: final runs of released models ~7 % of all compute; ~90 % of R&D went to experiments and unreleased runs
durable_properties.design_consequence: even training demand arrives as thousands of independent jobs: the sail-sized job is the natural unit.

durable_properties.property: Per-sequence working state is ~1-100 GB and stable
durable_properties.numbers: KV/token fell x0.35/yr (4.7 MB -> 8 KB) while context grew x3/yr (2k -> 1M); state at max context 1.3-68 GB since 2020
durable_properties.design_consequence: an agent's memory fits in 1-10 film chiplets (2070, 8 GB each); memory per agent, not per parameter, sizes chiplet NVM.

durable_properties.numbers: N ~ C^0.5 (Chinchilla); 1e28 replica state ~1.1-1.4 PB stays flat while sails grow: need 2e-7 vs supply 1.5e-4 B/(FLOP/s) in 2070
durable_properties.design_consequence: training never again needs HBM pods once film NVM exists; any sail holds hundreds of replicas.

durable_properties.property: Sparsity rises and is cheap on NVM
durable_properties.numbers: 3.6 -> 32 total/active in 2023-2025; idle experts in NVM cost zero standby power
durable_properties.design_consequence: capacity (GB per chiplet) matters more than bandwidth for weights; favours the film's stacked NVM.

durable_properties.property: Critical batch grows with data, not model size
durable_properties.design_consequence: larger runs get more parallel per step, so one sail stays compute-bound (1.6-21 s steps); the cross-sail latency wall is 3e29-7e33 FLOP/yr at a 1 s step floor.

durable_properties.numbers: DiLoCo >100x (H=30-500), SparseLoCo 97-99 % sparse + 2-bit, Covenant >146x; penalty +1.1 % loss at M=8
durable_properties.design_consequence: cross-sail training needs 1e-4-4e-2 of a sail's lasers: bandwidth is not the limit, the replica penalty is.

durable_properties.property: Verification-friendly search scales with independent samples
durable_properties.numbers: coverage log-linear over 1e4x samples; ES needs ~12 B per evaluation (~1e-10 of a sail's lasers)
durable_properties.design_consequence: 1e16+ loosely coupled sails have a use: search, self-play, evolution, ensembles.

durable_properties.numbers: compute-optimal ~7-8 bit integer; FP4 training demonstrated; accumulators 16-32 bit
durable_properties.design_consequence: at most ~2x more from precision after 2030 (already in study 1); FP64 science costs 16-60x per op.

durable_properties.property: Agents need general-purpose compute beside the model
durable_properties.design_consequence: every chiplet (or 1 in N) needs a sandbox-capable core, MMU and NVM main memory, or pods stay ~15 %.

durable_properties.property: Human data runs out at ~1e28-1e29 FLOP
durable_properties.numbers: 3e14 tokens (1e14-1e15); a 2070 sail-year run needs 1.6-7x that; 1e32 needs 60-270x
durable_properties.design_consequence: beyond one sail-year, data is generated by the swarm (rollouts, simulation, self-play): another reason generation dominates.

invalid_assumptions.assumption: Pods for DRAM-capacity CPU work (agent sandboxes, RL environments)
invalid_assumptions.verdict: valid to ~2045, then invalid if chiplets carry a general-purpose core + NVM main memory
invalid_assumptions.why: Demand is rising (CPU 4-12 % of AI power in 2026, forecast 14-48 %), so this driver grows before it disappears. Film NVM 1/8/32 GB per chiplet hosts a 0.5-8 GB sandbox on 1-8 chiplets from 2045-2070.
invalid_assumptions.replacement: Sandbox-capable film chiplets (MRAM/FeRAM main memory, MMU, microVM isolation); pods only for >~3.8 W dies and write-heavy DRAM work.

invalid_assumptions.assumption: Pods for storage, datasets, checkpoints, weight stores
invalid_assumptions.why: A 2070 sail holds 0.85 EB (0.41 x all HBM ever shipped by 2025); NVM weights survive brownouts, so the backing store and reload path disappear (study 2).
invalid_assumptions.replacement: Distributed film NVM; glass archives (Project Silica class) for cold data, ~0.01-0.1 % of power.

invalid_assumptions.assumption: Pods as training islands and a hedge (HBM)
invalid_assumptions.why: Training state per FLOP/s is 90-2,000x below film supply from 2040. With photonic lanes, MoE all-to-all costs 2-5 % of energy (study 3).
invalid_assumptions.replacement: The sail is the training island: a 1e28 run in ~20 days (2070), 7e28 FLOP per sail-year.

invalid_assumptions.assumption: Film for inference and 2D-TP training only
invalid_assumptions.why: Photonic lanes make all-to-all sail-wide (3e-4-6e-4 B/FLOP). Film patches serve 1e12-active models single-stream at 3.5-4.9e4 tok/s, as fast as a pod.
invalid_assumptions.replacement: Film for all synchronous work inside a sail: dense, MoE, RL learners, serving, tool execution.

invalid_assumptions.assumption: Inference dominates future demand (plausible, not established)
invalid_assumptions.verdict: now better supported; the distinction blurs at swarm scale
invalid_assumptions.why: Inference share 26 % (2024) -> ~50 % (2025) -> ~67 % forecast (2026). RL rollouts, search and synthetic data are inference-shaped.
invalid_assumptions.replacement: Forward-pass-shaped compute is 80-95 % of swarm FLOPs (speculation on measured anchors).

invalid_assumptions.assumption: Film's latency-bound decode edge only helps in-swarm agents
invalid_assumptions.verdict: valid, and at swarm scale nearly all consumers are in-swarm agents
invalid_assumptions.why: Earth is 200-1,200 s away and receives <1e-15 of swarm output (5e8 tok/s for all of Google in 2025 vs ~1e25 tok/s).
invalid_assumptions.replacement: Design for agent-to-agent loops inside a sail (decode floor 12-17 us per token in a patch).

invalid_assumptions.assumption: Low-communication training at swarm scale is unproven
invalid_assumptions.why: Evidence reaches 4.75e23 FLOP and M<=8-16 replicas; decentralized runs grow 20x/yr vs frontier 5x/yr. Bandwidth across 1e2-1e5 sails is ample.
invalid_assumptions.replacement: Plan for 1e2-1e5-sail islands (1e30-1e33 effective FLOP/yr) as speculative upside; no single model spans the swarm.

invalid_assumptions.assumption: FP8 dense FLOP as the unit; J/op is the lever
invalid_assumptions.why: Precision floor near 4-8 bits; FP64 science costs 16-60x per op.
invalid_assumptions.replacement: Report FP8-equivalent FLOP; tag science workloads separately.

invalid_assumptions.assumption: Global shuffles need a switched fabric in pods
invalid_assumptions.why: Film photonic global bit 0.11 pJ vs pod fabric 0.5-0.8 pJ (2070).

sail_as_unit.answer: Yes, the original intuition holds if 'satellite' means the sail. Synchronous chips should share one satellite. The satellite is the 279 m sail, and photonic lanes concentrate it logically, not physically. By 2050-2070 the sail is one tightly coupled 14.8 MW machine: 0.9 us mean and 2.75 us worst latency, 3e-4-6e-4 B/FLOP all-to-all, and NVLink-class bandwidth flat in distance. A physically dense pod buys nothing for synchronous work. Its switched-fabric collectives (0.1-1 us) and 2 km pod islands (6.7 us) are no faster. It costs 8x more mass per watt (4.0 vs 0.5 g/W, study 4).
sail_as_unit.what_concentrated_means_by_2070: Concentration splits into three meanings. (1) Coupling: chips that can share per-layer collectives at microsecond latency. That is the sail, or a 3-12 m patch inside it when a token must take under ~20 us. (2) Thermal concentration: dies above ~3.8 W. Only these belong in pods: fast single-thread cores, switch ASICs, cryostats. (3) Radiation shielding: DRAM, NAND and qubits. Workloads need (1) everywhere and (2)-(3) for only ~1-3 % of power.

architecture_implications.question: 1. Which workload properties are durable enough to design around; which architecture.md assumptions survive 10-1000x memory per chip, cheaper links and new algorithms?
architecture_implications.answer: Durable: generation-dominated compute; many independent jobs; ~1-100 GB working state per sequence; falling state per training FLOP; rising sparsity; critical batch growing with data; 100-1,000x low-comm compression with a replica penalty; agents' need for general-purpose sandboxes; a precision floor at 4-8 bit; human data exhausted at ~1e28-1e29 FLOP. Survive: film as the majority, sail as the synchronous unit, low-comm between sails, a small pod tier. Fail: pods for storage, training islands and shuffles (2040-2070). Pods for sandboxes survive only until chiplets can host them.
architecture_implications.numbers: see durable_properties and invalid_assumptions; training need 2e-7 vs film supply 1.5e-4 B/(FLOP/s) (2070); agents need ~1.5e-4 (1.5e-5-1.5e-2).

architecture_implications.question: 2. Pod share per era from workload reasons, combined with studies 2-3
architecture_implications.answer: Workload-driven p50 11.9 % / 2.3 % / 1.0 %; combined 12.7 % (7.8 %-24.5 %) / 2.6 % (1.6 %-5.7 %) / 1.1 % (0.6 %-2.4 %) for 2040/2070/2100+. That is about 2.5x studies 2-3 (5/1/0.3 %), because agentic CPU work is a rising share. If chiplets cannot run sandboxes it stays ~15 % (6-33 %) in every era.
architecture_implications.numbers: recommended visualizer values 12 % (2040), 2.5 % (2070), 1 % (2100+); each +1 % pods = +5.4-7.4 % swarm mass.

architecture_implications.question: 3. What does 'concentrated' mean when the sail is one tightly coupled 15 MW machine?
architecture_implications.answer: Yes, the original intuition holds if 'satellite' means the sail. Synchronous chips should share one satellite. The satellite is the 279 m sail, and photonic lanes concentrate it logically, not physically. By 2050-2070 the sail is one tightly coupled 14.8 MW machine: 0.9 us mean and 2.75 us worst latency, 3e-4-6e-4 B/FLOP all-to-all, and NVLink-class bandwidth flat in distance. A physically dense pod buys nothing for synchronous work. Its switched-fabric collectives (0.1-1 us) and 2 km pod islands (6.7 us) are no faster. It costs 8x more mass per watt (4.0 vs 0.5 g/W, study 4).
architecture_implications.numbers: Concentration splits into three meanings. (1) Coupling: chips that can share per-layer collectives at microsecond latency. That is the sail, or a 3-12 m patch inside it when a token must take under ~20 us. (2) Thermal concentration: dies above ~3.8 W. Only these belong in pods: fast single-thread cores, switch ASICs, cryostats. (3) Radiation shielding: DRAM, NAND and qubits. Workloads need (1) everywhere and (2)-(3) for only ~1-3 % of power.

architecture_implications.question: 4. What should the visualizer say the swarm computes?
architecture_implications.answer: Mostly a population, not a monolith. At f=0.01 with 2070 logic: 1.9e38 FLOP/s and 3.4e16 sails. That is ~2e23 human-brain equivalents (2e21-2e25), ~2.5e23 frontier-class agents and 1.3e25 tokens/s (2.6e16 x Google 2025). Each sail could run a 1e28-FLOP training run every ~20 days. The largest single model is 7e28 FLOP/yr per sail, and 1e30-1e33 only if low-comm training scales 7-10 orders of magnitude beyond today's evidence. Science: 60-230 exascale machines per sail.

architecture_implications.question: Design rules from workloads
architecture_implications.answer: (a) Give every chiplet, or 1 in N, a sandbox-capable core with MMU and NVM main memory: worth 10-30 % of swarm mass. (b) Size chiplet NVM by agent working sets, not training state. Take the high end (8-32 GB in 2070) if agents dominate. (c) Keep sails at 150-300 m. Each is a 1e21-1e22 FLOP/s island holding thousands of model replicas and ~1e7 agents. (d) Lasers: 1e-4-4e-2 of capacity for cross-sail training. The rest goes to policy broadcast (~350 TB per update, ~6 s per terminal) and agent traffic. (e) Pods only for dies above ~3.8 W, radiation-intolerant memory, cryogenic/quantum devices and archives.
